rules: Scope: only events on the two watchlists above, in the next US trading session (including that session's after-close reports). At most 3 events per run and at most 2 calls per event, 5 calls per run in total.

Earnings calls: (a) 'TICKER moves more than its implied move on the reaction session' and (b) 'TICKER closes the reaction session up'. The reaction session is the next session for after-close reports and the same session for pre-open reports; the move is close to close, measured from the last close before the report.

Implied move: an options-based figure for the reaction session (a quoted straddle or 'options imply' figure, or a real chain if one is available), with its source and date. If none can be found, use the stock's average absolute reaction over its last 4 to 8 reports, label it 'hist', and say so in the preview. Never make one up.

Macro calls: (a) 'the headline figure prints above consensus' (equal to consensus is a miss) and (b) 'the S&P 500 moves more than the VIX-implied one-day move on release day' (implied = prior VIX close / sqrt(252), in %; realized = |ln(close/prev)| x 100).

Baselines (prob_base, no judgment): earnings big move = the engine's own measured rate once 10 earnings big-move calls are graded, before that an assumed prior of 0.40, flagged as assumed. Earnings up = 0.50. Macro above consensus = 0.50. S&P bigger than implied = the share of Desk Daily days docs where realized_pct > implied_pct (all days on file).

Desk view: prob_raw is the engine's judgment from the evidence (guidance history, positioning, the stock's run-up into the report, nowcasts, the last few prints). Then calibrate it exactly as the desk does (method/notes rule 2, using Desk Daily meta/scoreboard calibration bins), and set the final prob = average of prob_adj and prob_base until 20 engine calls are graded; after that, weight them by inverse trailing Brier over the last 40 graded engine calls. Store prob_raw, prob_adj, prob_base and prob.
Pull tails toward 50%: no engine call above 80% or below 20%.

Post-mortem (within one run of the reaction session's close): record the actual figure or reaction, implied vs actual move, grade the engine's calls on verified numbers only, and write two sentences: what the market cared about and whether the preview's reasoning held. Never grade on conflicting figures; leave the call open and say why.

Data order: FMP (index and mega-cap prices work on the current plan; small and mid caps and the earnings calendar do not), then official sources (BLS, BEA, Census, ISM, the Fed, company IR releases), then web search. Flag single-sourced figures. Bigdata.com and Financial Datasets were out of credits on 26 Nov; try them, and if they refuse, say so in the run summary and move on.
Analysis only. Never suggest a trade or position. The paper book does not trade event calls.
